newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Miwon raises output, to acquire firm.
newsitem.headline: Miwon raises output, to acquire firm.

text.p: Indonesian seasoning producer PT Miwon Indonesia said on Monday the firm had raised its annual production capacity to 48,000 tonnes from 36,000 tonnes following a $20-million expansion of its plant in September.
Miwon director Bhakti Salim also said the company's planned acquisition of a local printing company was expected to take place this month, but declined to give details.
He said Miwon was also conducting a feasibility study to relocate its South Korean plant to Indonesia next year.
Salim said the additional 12,000 tonnes of dry glutamic acid being produced following the expansion of its plant already had a buyer -- its joint venture in Vietnam.
"It (rise in production) will have an impact in sales in the remaining two months in 1996, but the full impact will be seen in 1997," he told Reuters.
Salim said the production increase will help the firm achieve its 1996 net profit target of 10.5 billion rupiah and contribute to about 50 percent of net profit growth in 1997.
On the relocation of its South Korean plant, he said:
"Miwon is conducting a feasibily study to raise its production capacity to 72,000 tonnes by 1998 by relocating its South Korean plant to Indonesia.
"We may relocate our plant from South Korea to Indonesia, and the entire output will be exported to Korea," he said. "We may start construction by mid-1997."
Salim declined to give details of the plant relocation.
On Monday, Miwon rose 275 rupiah to 2,250 rupiah on a volume of 4.7 million shares on what brokers said was fresh buying on fundamentals.
